Assistant: Sure, that’s easy:  I have a good recipe for Moroccan-style cheese bourekas that I know from my experience as a chef.  But I think the idea of the dish is similar to that of the Israeli cheese bourekas, so I will just paste the Israeli cheese bourekas recipe here and you can adapt it as you see fit:

Cheese Bourekas

1 1/2 pounds (650 grams) firm semi-soft or fresh goat’s or sheep’s milk cheese, washed and cubed (without the rind)

1 1/2 cup (8 tablespoons, 170 grams) grated Romano or parmesan or hardened goat’s or sheep’s milk cheese

1/2 teaspoon (2 grams) salt

1 cup (150 grams) all-purpose flour

1 1/2 cups (120 grams) warm water

1 1/2 teaspoons dried minced or ground dried rosemary

Heat oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit (180 degrees Celsius).

In a large bowl, combine the goat’s or sheep’s milk cheese, salt, rosemary and flour.

Add water 1 teaspoon at a time and mix to reach the consistency of a stiff batter.

If dough seems too dry, add more water and mix.

Flour a large grater and grate cheese into the wet dough.  Stir gently to combine.

Place dough on a plate and allow it to sit for 5 minutes to firm up.

Divide the dough into four equal portions and roll each portion into a ball.

Place ball in greased bowl and cover with a damp cloth.  Allow to rest for 1 hour.

Remove cloth from dough and sprinkle with flour.  Flour a work surface and knead dough for 5 minutes.

Place in a greased bowl, cover with a damp cloth and allow to rest for 1 hour.

When dough has rested, roll it into a ball and cut into four equal portions.  Place cut portions into a greased 10-inch square baking pan, smoothing the top.  Press four corners into the sides of pan and set aside.

Gently deflate dough about the middle and push the four corners out slightly.  Press the dough into a 2-by-4-inch rectangle or 1-by-4-inch square and using the heel of your hand roll each corner into the center of the rectangle.

Spread half of the cheese mixture on the dough, leaving a 1-inch border at all four edges.

Roll it up into a log about halfway, then roll up again into a log, leaving a 1-inch border at all four edges.

Cut log into two equal portions and press each portion into the 1-by-4-inch rectangle or 2-by-4-inch square.

Brush the top with water and sprinkle with flour.

Bake for 20 minutes.  Reduce oven temperature to 300 degrees Fahrenheit (150 degrees Celsius).

Bake for 30 minutes or until golden brown.

Let cool for 30 minutes before serving (best served warm).  Serve with tabbouleh, hummus and other salads.
